Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Jul 21, 12:49 pm, Ben Swainbank <vtesst...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> A leader has risen. The Camarilla have appointed a new commander to
> lead them. The Imperator has been chosen.

As always, thanks for setting these up. They are always fun.

It seems like it was inevitable that Karsh was going to be made
Imperator, due to the way that the rules worked. He was the only
minion that was named/mentioned in the set up as someone specifically
you could vote for as Imperator, so likely end result is a few people
vote for Karsh, as is specifically laid out as a special option, and
everyone else just votes for some random vampire. Did any other minion
get more than, like, 2 votes for Imperator?

Not that this is remotely bad (Karsh is as good an Imperator as anyone
else, I guess). But I'd suggest that in future Storyline events, where
there is going to be a vote for something at the end of each
tournament, there be more inherent limits placed on the voting. Like
for example, for this event, if instead of "Karsh, or anyone else",
you could vote for "Karsh, or a specific named minion based on your
clan" (i.e. everyone who won with Ventrue voted automatically for, say
Gotsdam) and then in the set up, an Imperator Nominee was listed for
each Camarilla clan. Or something like that. To make the voting/
selection a bit more controllable.

-Peter

> Gotsdam) and then in the set up, an Imperator Nominee was listed for
> each Camarilla clan. Or something like that. To make the voting/
> selection a bit more controllable.
>

But this wouldn't have really changed the voting. You could vote for
a minion of your choice from your clan, but your vote still counted
towards your clan. If Brujah had received the most votes, and Count
Germaine had the most votes, even if it was only 2 votes, then
Germaine would have won. I fail to see how your proposal would have
been better in any way, in that it would allow players to decide the
clan who won, but would give them 0 input on which vampire, as opposed
to the current way which lets you have at least some say in the
specific vampire.

Personally, I would have preferred it if Gangrel had simply been a
playable clan. Perhaps Karsh would have been the only allowed
Imperator nominee for Gangrel, but I think I would have liked having 7
clans instead of only 6 to choose from.

All in all, though, I liked the way this turned out, and I enjoyed
being able to play Malkavians without having to *choose* Malkavians.

Messages.Author: echia...@yahoo.com
Messages.Body:


Excellent aftermath! I really enjoyed reading the conclusion. Some
points:

+ I liked how the story put a reasonable explanation of how Germaine
could be nominated. Dmitra provided an ample explanation which was
logical, even if it was clear that not everyone genuinely believed in
it. And at the same time, the story was consistent with Germaine's
character. No, he was NOT infiltrating the Anarchs on behalf of the
Camarilla, he was actually trying to do the exact opposite!

+ Also nice that they included Madame Guil. Showing her reaction and
explaining the situation was critical to making Germaine's appearance
(and nomination) plausible.

+ Liked the nod to how Karsh had been "Absent for so long everyone
assumed he was dead." (Potential tongue-in-cheek reference to rumors
that Karsh had been staked at the bottom of the ocean). Would have
been nice to see Theo Bell's reaction when Karsh showed up (though
once again the novels are only pseudo-canon at best).

+ I also thought that the brief portrayal of Karsh was also fairly
consistent with his personality (quiet and calm).

+ For those who actually believe in the Karsh = Jalan theory (once
again, most of the canon source material contradicts the account
during that twilight Gehenna-era novel), the story was vague enough,
that you could theorize that maybe the Black Hand set up this
situation, just so that Karsh/Jalan becomes Imperator. Everyone gets
so focused on the obvious strawman threat (Germaine) that they flock
to Karsh, who could be the actual danger (if you think he actually is
Jalan). So the story is flexible that you can believe whatever you
want (such insidious Black Hand schemes! Germaine himself suspects a
setup!).

+ There's also a nice continuity from the previous storylines (Anarchs
and Alastors with Germaine and Yazid. Even a mention of Lucinde's
previous appearance. And then mixing in the Helena storyline and
flowing into the next upcoming storyline event).

+ For those who missed it, the precession of names following the Inner
Circle included most of the Key Minions who had supported Karsh.
Originally I was puzzled by the motley list of names (including many
Princes). But if you check the standings, Anson, Gilbert Duane, Sir
Walter Nash, Gustav BREIDENSTEIN, Santaleous, Rachel Brandywine,
Anastasz di Zagreb, Ellison Humboldt, Sergei Voshkov, Jann Berger, and
Valerius Maior (along with Hardestadt) were all Key Minions selected
by the winning players who supported Karsh.

- It's a bit of a shame that the handful of other key minions who
supported Karsh didn't get a mention. Astrid Thomas could have been
added to the procession. Ohana and Amelia could have been in the
crowd. And maybe even some clandestine support from Hunters (Carlton)
could have gotten in there. But at least they got most of the
mentions.

- Nit-picking, but I would have liked it slightly more if the order of
clans supporting Karsh was represented of how much they actually
supported him in the tournaments. Malkavians did provide the most
support (5), but second was Tremere (4), followed by both Brujah (3)
and Nosferatu (3). The Ventrue (2) and Toreador (1) actually provided
the least amount of support. So it would have been nice if the Tremere
and Nosferatu had supported Karsh before the Ventrue and Toreador did.

- The major problem I saw was a LOT of spelling, grammar, and editing
mistakes. Could have used another read through or two. Hopefully a
cleaned up copy can be posted. But I'll give the storyline team the
benefit of the doubt and assume they wanted the players to know the
results ASAP.

? The Helena portion mentioned Claudia and Rodrigo. Who are they?

? Valerius Maior's appearance could lead to some rather interesting
possibilities. (Also, not sure why Germaine was so surprised to see
Jann Berger. If anything, Voshkov's appearance would probably have
been more surprising, given that he's Baba Yaga's minion).

? If Karsh has been absent so long that people think he's dead, then
why did everyone seem to know about him during the Prologue? The
Tremere meeting specifically mentions Karsh and considers how the
clans might rally behind him. So it seems odd that many in the
Camarilla might think he's dead. Then again, the best explanation I
can come up with is that *Germaine* believes he's dead and he has very
limited information (the Camarilla higher-ups all know Karsh is
around, not to mention the Tremere might have extra info due to their
mystic resources).

But overall, excellent work by Ben and the rest of the storyline team!
Looking forward to the next storyline event (though hopefully not
*too* soon!).

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Jul 21, 3:37 pm, XZealot <xzea...@cox.net> wrote:
> It was really the most reasonable solution.
>

>
> What could be more fair?

I'm not saying it wasn't fair. I'm saying that given the set up of the
event, it seemed *really* unlikely that anyone other than Karsh was
going to "win". I mean, maybe the intended result was "make sure Karsh
becomes Imperator", but maybe not. And if the intended result was
"maybe someone other than Karsh becomes Imperator", I don't think the
set up really enabled that.

To be clear here--I honestly don't care one way or the other who
Imperator is, and Karsh "winning" is just as good of a result in my
eyes as anyone else would have been "winning" (i.e. the storyline of
the game world isn't something I am remotely invested in, but I like
storyline tournaments anyway). But in terms of the mechanics
presented, I struck me from day one that the end result was mostly pre-
determined (i.e. the "winner" was going to be Karsh). I'd like to see,
in the future for an event like this, a less predetermined end result.
Not 'cause the end result here was bad, but 'cause it seemed like it
was inevitable.

-Peter

I, for one, actually liked the system and mechanics used for
determining the Imperator. The mechanics showed not only the struggle
between clans, but also the political divisions within clans.

Peter, I thought it was anything but "inevitable." Up until the very
end (especially the last week or two), it was a very tight race
between Karsh and the Brujah (who had a dominant lead during most of
the time). In fact, the amount of Brujah wins (in particular,
supporting Germaine) was quite impressive!

As Chris already mentioned, the total clan votes were far more
important that the individual votes (which just determined the leading
candidate within the clan). And actually, several vampires got more
than 2 votes. Germaine got an impressive 6 votes (out of 14 Brujah).
Both Roxanne and The Ankou each got 3 votes (of the 7 Malkavian wins)
- seems reasonable that they settled their internal conflict by going
with Karsh! Gerald Windham got 3 votes (half of the 6 Tremere wins),
while Democritus also got 3 (out of 8 Ventrue wins).

Having an open-ended nomination process allowed greater flexibility,
where players had more say and could influence the storyline. The
sheer amount of support for Germaine (and his heavy involvement in the
Aftermath) is testament to how the players helped shape the story
(along with the actual win for Karsh).

I thought the way they handled Karsh, was perfect. Obviously, there
are some basic storyline factors (Gangrel have left the Camarilla.
Imperator sounds awfully like the Warlord role, so if would be
puzzling if Karsh was NOT mentioned). And it gives you an option to
play a clan, while not necessarily supporting that clan (sleazy Malks,
etc). Having the Gangrel as a playable faction would have been
difficult, especially since most of the recent crypt cards are
Independent, and the theme of the event was Camarilla-centric, so I
can understand that decision. Plus, it would have been too big of an
advantage for Karsh. (And I like being able to support Karsh, without
playing Gangrel.)

Although there have previously been complaints about the slanted odds
with both the Nergal and the Anarch wins, at least this one actually
makes sense! Sure, there was some king making in the end (especially
when it got to Germaine vs Karsh). But as mentioned in the very
introduction:

"One of the biggest motivations for any clan to put forward an
Imperator is to prevent the others from getting too much power. Should
Karsh present himself, he may very well get the votes of any clan
whose own nominee is eliminated."

That's exactly what happened. In the end, the clans who had no chance
of winning it for themselves decided to support Karsh rather than
letting the Brujah or Ventrue win it. So it mirrors the sort of
political machinations that were almost certainly present in the
Camarilla's actual (fictional) voting process.

Again, the way the rules were set up, you had a choice between voting
for:

A) Karsh
B) Not Karsh

Votes for "Not Karsh" were going to be split all over the place, by
virtue of clan. Votes for "Karsh" were going to be both for Karsh and
taking away votes for Not Karsh. Some people were going to abandon
their winning clan and voting for Karsh, simply because it was an
option (and was cool, or whatever). Which means that the clans that
won were going to lose votes. Meaning that, in all likelihood, Karsh
was going to win the vote. Which might have been the intended result.
And is fine. But again, it struck me as kind of inevitable.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:


I swear that there was a different post from LSJ in this thread before
that I wanted to reply to, but if so, I guess it was cancelled and
replaced with this one (or I was imagining things).

But whoever posted it said "When the choice is X versus (write-in), X
tends to win." And that would be true if each vote for a vampire
counted equally and the vampire with the most votes won. That's not
how the voting worked. The way it worked was that you, essentially,
had 6 choices. Your choice was based on the clan that you played, so
one would think that most of the time, people picked a clan they
liked, and possibly even a clan that they want more goodies for. If
you won, then you had the choice of defecting from your choice to
(X).

I think the strongest conjecture that you can make regarding the
"fixing" of the results, is that Karsh had a better than 1 in 7 chance
of winning (that is, giving him as a choice to each of the other 6
clans gives him a better chance than if Gangrel had simply been one of
the 7 playable factions) - perhaps you could say better than 1 in 6,
since he would probably be more likely to win than any 1 other clan.
Saying that he was inevitable, or even greater than the combined
chances of all other clans would demand knowledge of people's decision
making processes that you just couldn't have.

If you look at it a different way, you are dividing people into 2
groups: A) Those who would vote for their own clan (which would be
subdivided into 6 groups), and B) Those who would vote for Karsh. You
can't really say much about the size of either of those groups, but if
you assume that people are reasonably close to evenly divided between
which clan they "like", then you could say that group B is at least as
large as A/6.

However, say you divide people into 2 different groups: A) Those who
want to "mess" with the story and have a silly or stupid result. B)
Those who don't fit in group A. From posts on the newsgroup, we know
that people existed in group A. I won't necessarily classify a win
for Valerius Maior or Count Germaine as a person in group A, but they
are someone who *might* be in group A, since those vamps don't really
make sense for Imperator without some twisting. But say we have those
2 groups. The people in group A would not vote for Karsh, since
voting for the one choice specifically given to you by the storyline
coordinator could hardly be "messing" with the results. So everyone
in group A would not vote for Karsh, and group B would be split
between people voting for Karsh and people voting for the clan they
decided to play.

From this, since A = Not Karsh, and B = some Karsh mixed in among
votes for the other 6 clans, you can conclude that Karsh could never
have won. It was fixed from the beginning. Of course, you see the
fallacy in that argument, in that we have no idea of the size of group
A, and could easily conjecture that it is small in relation to group
B...

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
Looking at the system, it was designed so that Karsh would split every
clan's vote.

"I could vote for Vamp A from Clan X, or Karsh..." is the decision
from each clan. So when you then have that there is a potentially
LARGE pool of "Vamp As" there is an impression that there would be a
small chance for your "Chosen Vamp A" to be the front-runner of Clan
X. So you vote for an unknown quantity (by backing Clan X and seeing
which Vamp A comes out on top from Clan X)... or back the very well
known quantity, Karsh.

Consequently, those who instinctively dislike the "punting for my Vamp
A from Clan X to win" would nominate Karsh. Also, after some results
and nominations came in those people who disliked the vampires coming
out for their favourite Clan X... they would also "sabotage" Clan X
and vote Karsh.

Think of it a bit like this...

There is "The Conservative Party", "The Moderate Party", "The
Environmental Loonies Party" and "Barack Obama" in an election. If
you choose one of the parties, they will choose the next President.
If you choose Barack Obama, he becomes President. If you don't trust
the parties to choose a good president (even if you agree with the
ideals of that party) you would consider choosing Barack Obama because
you KNOW who the President would be. Consequently the "Obama Vote"
splits each of the parties and if the media talked about some really
"rogue crazies" being likely nominations for each party, people will
abandon the parties to vote "Obama" so they get a known quantity.

Consequently (using the example scenario) Karsh won. It was always a
likely event, not a dominatingly likely event... but a likely one.

only taking a win away from the Toreador if I had played Toreador
with the intetion of voting for Toreador, and then decided at the last
minute to instead give the win to the Gangrel for some reason. I doubt
that the latter happened much, though obviously I have no way to prove
that.

> Mind you, I'm not saying that Gangrel necessarily
> had an advantage because of this, just that there is a bias one way or
> another.

I don't understand what you mean here. If you agree that people who
voted for Gangrel to win would most likely have played Gangrel if that
clan had been playable, what is the basis for the bias you perceive?

John Eno

I'd expect, actually, that the reason we had a significant late-cycle
surge in Gangrel wins (which we did, to some extent) was because, near
the end of the cycle, it was clearly between Gangrel and Brujah
starring Germaine. That means that whatever deck you wanted to play,
those were your only reasonable choices at that point - support
Gangrel, or let the Brujah win (assuming a non-Brujah player).

Think of it sort of like the difference in the presidential primary
season between living in New Hampshire, and living in Massachusetts.
Up there, where it's early, it's an open field; your vote gets to help
narrow it down to a much smaller field. Down here, well, the last two
election cycles the candidate I most supported wasn't even still in
the race by MA's primary time. So I was like a Toreador player. I
could play it anyway, and write in the vote for Toreador that'd be
meaningless; I could switch and play Brujah if I wanted Germaine to
win; or I could play the Toreador I wanted to play and, if I didn't
like Germaine for whatever reason, I could vote Gangrel.

- D.J.
